title: The Lord is with you, not an earthly bridegroom

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 12, cols. B-C (PDF p. 36)

source_text: Ideo et verbis illis, Ave gratia plena, primum Angelus ipsam salutando compellavit: Dominus tecum. Et non terrenus sponsus; sed ipse sanctificationis Dominus, pater castitatis, incorruptionis auctor, et libertatis dator; salutis procurator, et verae pacis conservator, atque largitor: qui ex terra virgine creavit hominem, et ex illius latere ac costa Evam assumpsit: Hic Dominus tecum, et rursum ex te.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore also with those words, Hail full of grace, first the Angel, greeting (salutando) her, addressed (compellavit): The Lord with you. And not an earthly bridegroom (terrenus sponsus); but the very Lord of sanctification (sanctificationis Dominus), father of chastity (pater castitatis), author of incorruption (incorruptionis auctor), and giver of freedom (libertatis dator); manager/procurer of salvation (salutis procurator), and preserver (conservator) and bestower (largitor) of true peace (vera pax): who from virgin earth (terra virgo) created (creavit) man (homo), and from his side (latus) and rib (costa) took up (assumpsit) Eve: This Lord with you, and again (rursum) from you.

choices.choice: 'sanctificationis Dominus' rendered 'the Lord of holiness'; the same choice is used for sanctificatio in section 13 (margin variant 'al. sanctitatis', 'holiness', gives the same sense).
'pater castitatis' kept lower-case, as in the print: a title of the Lord, not the First Person.
'ex terra virgine creavit hominem' alludes to Genesis 2:7 (Adam from untilled earth) and 'ex illius latere ac costa Evam' to Genesis 2:21-22; both cited.
'rursum ex te' rendered 'in turn comes from you'.
Margin variant 'al. protulit, creavit' at 'assumpsit' not adopted.

pass_b_english: Therefore with those words, Hail, full of grace, the Angel first greeted her and addressed her: The Lord is with you (Luke 1:28). Not an earthly bridegroom, but the Lord of holiness Himself, the father of chastity, the author of incorruption and the giver of freedom; the one who brings about salvation, and the keeper and giver of true peace; who created man from the virgin earth (Genesis 2:7), and took Eve from his side and rib (Genesis 2:21-22): this Lord is with you, and in turn comes from you.
notes: 'sanctificationis Dominus' rendered 'the Lord of holiness'; the same choice is used for sanctificatio in section 13 (margin variant 'al. sanctitatis', 'holiness', gives the same sense). 'pater castitatis' kept lower-case, as in the print: a title of the Lord, not the First Person. 'ex terra virgine creavit hominem' alludes to Genesis 2:7 (Adam from untilled earth) and 'ex illius latere ac costa Evam' to Genesis 2:21-22; both cited. 'rursum ex te' rendered 'in turn comes from you'. Margin variant 'al. protulit, creavit' at 'assumpsit' not adopted.
